pr_body:
"flags" is a common variable name and is more likely to be passed to LOG_DBG() or LOG_ERR() as a parameter. Changing the name of the local variable created in Z_LOG_MSG_STACK_CREATE() from "flags" to "_options" make it less likely that someone will pass a parameter of that name to LOG_DBG() or LOG_ERR() and have that passed value occluded by the variable created in Z_LOG_MSG_STACK_CREATE.

Fixes #57089

issue_context.title: Z_LOG_MSG_STACK_CREATE() variable "flags" hides that of caller
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The macro Z_LOG_MSG_STACK_CREATE() creates a local variable named "flags". Unfortunately, should someone invoke LOG_DBG() or LOG_ERR() and pass a parameter named "flags" (as is the case in kernel/mmu.c::z_phys_map()) then the macro's copy of the "flags" variable will override/occlude that of the caller.

Please also mention any information which could help others to understand
the problem you're facing:
This was found via Coverity.

**To Reproduce**
Inspect.

**Expected behavior**
The macro Z_LOG_MSG_STACK_CREATE() should probably not be using a common variable name such as "flags". I would recommend changing the name to have a leading underscore so that it becomes "_flags".

**Impact**
This is a minor issue. It only shows up in a couple of corner cases.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Any
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK

review_comments: Side note: Originally I tried using "_flags" instead of "_options". However, this led to build warnings stating that "_flags" was initialised but not used. That warning is thought to come from a separate instance of "_flags" elsewhere in the chain of macros that comprise LOG_DBG().
